name: tbox (coroutine channel)
baseline: Go channels (GOMAXPROCS=1), libmill channels, libtask, libgo (boost), libfiber (acl)
workload: 10,000,000 values passed through a coroutine channel from one coroutine to another, unbuffered (size 0) and with a 10000-element buffer, one scheduler thread, in the benchbox 'channel' test.
claimed_speedup: Unbuffered, LinuxMint x86_64 VM: tbox 1702 ms vs libmill 2298 ms, golang 5343 ms, libfiber 4452 ms, libgo(boost) 11391 ms, libtask 12894 ms (derived from page data: about 1.35x vs libmill, 3.1x vs Go). Unbuffered, macOS x86_64: tbox 916 ms vs golang 3180 ms, libmill 3460 ms, libtask 3646 ms (derived from page data: about 3.5x vs Go, 3.8x vs libmill). Buffer 10000, LinuxMint x86_64 VM: tbox 293 ms vs golang 782 ms, libmill 1135 ms, libgo 1362 ms, libfiber 1510 ms, libtask 1528 ms (derived from page data: about 2.7x vs Go, 3.9x vs libmill). Buffer 10000, macOS x86_64: tbox 404 ms vs golang 1135 ms, libtask 2785 ms, libmill 4401 ms (derived from page data: about 2.8x vs Go).
hardware: VirtualBox VMs (ArchLinux i386, LinuxMint x86_64, Windows XP and Win7 for tbox only) and macOS x86_64; CPU model not stated
tradeoffs: Channel is one module of tbox, a glib-like C library (streams, containers, coroutines, regex and more); the benchmark runs one tbox scheduler thread against Go with GOMAXPROCS(1), so no multi-core scaling is shown. Needs tbox's own coroutine scheduler and an xmake build; channel API is tb_co_channel_* and only works inside tbox coroutines.
caveats: First-party benchmark by the tbox author (benchbox repo, source at tboox/benchbox src/coroutine/channel/{tbox,libmill,go,libtask,libgo,libfiber}); no compiler, flags, library versions or CPU model stated, most rows are VM runs, code carries 2015-2017 copyright so numbers are old. Harness differences read in the sources: tbox runs sender and receiver as two coroutines on its scheduler and times only the scheduler loop, while libmill and Go send from main and receive in one spawned loop that never exits, so setup and teardown are not timed identically. The tbox repo is already in the catalog for the coroutine switch benchmark (id https://github.com/tboox/tbox, tier C, retiered because the Boost and libco switch rows bounce through main); this record is a separate claim from the same repo and needs a paper: id before merging. Numbers were read from the raw wiki markdown of the channel page.
found_via: seed-record pass: awesome-c Frameworks entry for TBOX (seed lead 'Multi-platform library with a large number of capabilities'), then github.com/waruqi/tbox, github.com/tboox/benchbox and its wiki channel page
